clue.text: Equipment for cutting out journalistic clichés

parts.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist, so a journalistic cliché is a hack's saying
saws are old sayings, worn-out proverbs

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a tool for stripping tired stock phrases out of newspaper copy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'journalistic clichés' as 'hack saws', the sayings of a hack; the surface makes you think of editing, not carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Saws with fine blades in a frame are the standard tools for cutting shapes out of metal or wood.

clue.text: Williams & Co are no longer managing

definitions.text: Williams & Co are no longer managing

parts.words: Williams & Co are no longer managing
parts.note: Kenneth Williams and fellow actors starred in the long British comedy film series whose titles began 'Carry On'; the phrase also means managing or continuing

explanation.surface: A firm called Williams & Co has ceased trading.
explanation.walkthrough: Williams & Co looks like a business name, but it is Kenneth Williams and the rest of the cast of the British 'Carry On' comedy films. The phrase in the answer also means 'managing' or 'continuing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going or manage, and the cast of that comic film series made their name doing it.

clue.text: Unmoved yet

definitions.meaning: as an adverb, nevertheless or even so

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both motionless and nevertheless, two unrelated senses of one adverb-adjective.

clue.text: See 11
Irritation only 75% can get along without

indicators.note: keeping only three quarters of an eight-letter word means dropping its last two letters

parts.note: something needless is something you can manage without

explanation.surface: A grumble that most people could cope perfectly well without being annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only 75%' keeps the first six of eight letters. 'Can get along without' reads like part of the sentence about the irritation, but it is a synonym for the eight-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle as a noun means provocation or irritation, as in 'there was needle between the teams'.

clue.text: Greek musician not all there in the City of the Gospel

indicators.note: the shortened musician's name goes inside the City's letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London

indicators.note: the musician's name is not complete, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: Vangelis is the Greek composer of the Chariots of Fire score

explanation.surface: A Greek composer behaving oddly in the City of London is called evangelical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all there' suggests madness but drops the S of VANGELIS; the City of London's postcode is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic is an adjective meaning relating to the Gospels or their teaching.

clue.text: The numbers are a bit stuck up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending the word upwards reads it backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the figures are slightly arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' looks like snobbish but turns A TAD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are figures or facts gathered for analysis, so numbers in a general sense.

clue.text: Score a century entering the ground

indicators.note: the century's letter goes into the middle of the rearranged word
ground means crushed and reshaped, so the letters of the word the are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman makes a hundred on arriving at the cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns THE into ETH; C goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to cut lines into a surface, which is what engraving with acid does.

clue.text: Impressive words I note — but not quite back on time

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it
reading the pieces backwards gives the start of the answer
the note's name falls one letter short

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone admits their grand words were a little late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last E of BREVE, giving BREV; 'back' turns I + BREV into VERBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbiage is wordy, inflated language meant to sound grand rather than say much.

clue.text: Ploy, with hearts only, to amass and retain the cards you've got

indicators.note: only the middle part of each word is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: to stack is to pile up or accumulate
in pontoon, to stick is to keep your hand and take no more cards

explanation.surface: A card player's scheme: play only hearts, gather tricks and keep what you hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts only' strips the ends of STACK and STICK, leaving TAC and TIC. 'Hearts' sounds like the suit or the card game, but it means the middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a scheme or manoeuvre used to gain an advantage, as a ploy is.

clue.text: Cunning goggle-wearer, good circler: come, it's who? I'm our inspiration's full entitlement

indicators.note: something cunning is crafty or contrived, so the following words are craftily rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle about a goggled airman circling overhead, asking who he is.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Biggles took the name from W E Johns's flying hero, whose name was in turn reputed to come from a real RAF officer. 'Cunning' shuffles all 35 letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's pseudonym honours a fictional pilot, and this is the full rank and name of the real officer said to have inspired it.

clue.text: Source of rallying cry of POs?

definitions.text: Source of rallying cry of POs?

indicators.note: the answer is the source the clue's later words come from when its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; POs are petty officers or pilot officers

explanation.surface: Asks where the petty officers' battle cry came from.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters rearranged give 'rallying cry of POs', so it is literally their source. It was the First World War air arm that came before the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: The First World War air service, forerunner of the RAF, fittingly had officers who might rally.

clue.text: Faint cries emitted by Pope, perhaps

indicators.note: letters given out are let loose and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The pontiff lets out weak cries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitted' rearranges FAINT CRIES. 'Faint' looks like it describes the cries, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pope canonises saints, so he is one who makes holy; the 'perhaps' marks him as one example.

clue.text: Rich source of oil on the list?

parts.note: an oil well is where oil comes from
a ship that lists leans over, or has heeled

explanation.surface: Asks whether a wealthy oil source has made it on to a list of rich people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a roll of names, but it is the nautical sense of leaning over, as a ship that has heeled.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an informal idiom for wealthy, from the idea of having good shoes.

clue.text: Cowboy's home cooking is done on it

definitions.meaning: the open grazing land of the American West, as in 'Home on the...'
a kitchen stove with hotplates and an oven

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both open grazing country and a kitchen stove, two unrelated nouns.

clue.text: Squeezing a pound from next girl to work

indicators.note: set to work, the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Wringing a pound out of the next girl to start a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the L away: NEXT GIRL TO shuffled gives the answer plus L. 'work' reworks the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Extorting is squeezing money out of someone by force or threats.

clue.text: Reaper's greeting time off work

parts.note: the reaper's tool, a curved blade for cutting corn, as carried by the Grim Reaper
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: The Grim Reaper says hello, so you take a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Reaper's' as 'the reaper's tool', the curved blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick leave is time off work granted because of illness.

clue.text: Exterior space — on the contrary, indoor space

parts.note: the front is the outward-facing side of something
room means space, as in 'room to move'

explanation.surface: An outside area is described, then corrected to an inside one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the contrary' does no work in the wordplay: the outside-sounding pieces make a room inside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A front room is a sitting room at the front of a house, an indoor living space.

clue.text: See 11
Turncoat going in to recover pointlessly working backwards

indicators.note: the turned coat goes into the shortened word for recover
a point is a compass letter like E, so one is removed

parts.note: to retrieve is to get back
read as 'turn coat': the four letters of coat turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A traitor goes into hiding to get things back aimlessly, working in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turncoat' wants to be RAT, but split it as 'turn coat', the letters of coat rearranged. 'pointlessly' drops one E (east, a compass point), and 'going in to' places one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroactive means taking effect from a date in the past, so it works backwards in time.

clue.text: See 12
Cold Mountain?

parts.note: the title of a novel and film, read literally as a mountain of ice floating in the sea

explanation.surface: Asks about the novel and film of that name.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold Mountain is a 1997 novel and 2003 film, but read literally it is a frozen peak, a short form of iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg is a floating mass of ice, literally a cold mountain at sea.

clue.text: The object of a woman's love?

definitions.text: The object of a woman's love?

parts.note: the object form of she, the pronoun for a woman, is her
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Asks who a woman loves.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the man a woman worships, or the legendary Greek woman Leander loved; in the wordplay, HER is the object pronoun for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's idol or champion is the man she looks up to and admires.

clue.text: All over article in church, producing unpleasant reaction

indicators.note: the whole assembled thing is turned over end to end
the article goes inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an item is an article or thing

explanation.surface: Something placed in a church causes nausea everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All over' sounds like 'everywhere' but reverses the whole container built by 'in', which reads CITEME before turning.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that makes you vomit, an unpleasant reaction.

clue.text: After reflection, Lord Lieutenant is to cross the threshold

indicators.note: seen in a mirror, the pieces read backwards

parts.note: LL abbreviates Lord Lieutenant, the monarch's representative in a British county
a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in rood screen

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, the county's royal representative steps through a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a verb with 'the threshold', but it is a noun, a crucifix. The Lord Lieutenant is the monarch's representative in a British county.
explanation.definitionFit: A sill at the foot of a door is the threshold you step over.

clue.text: See 11
Having removed the blue colour after being in company?

indicators.note: the colour comes after the rest
the word for being sits inside company's letters

parts.note: ens is a philosophical term for being or existence
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Describes someone who has lost their blue tint by being among others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' means smutty: a censor removes the blue material. ENS is a philosophers' word for being.
explanation.definitionFit: Censored material has had its obscene or blue content cut out.
